reason: While the text includes and prominently features the voices and grievances of working people (farmers and common laborers describing their debts, mortgaged properties, and enslaved children), the overall narrative is told from the perspective of Nehemiah, a government official serving as governor. The story is framed through his reaction to hearing their complaints ('And it was very displeasing to me when I heard their cry'), his judgment of the situation, his actions in confronting the nobles and officials, and his own righteousness as a leader who did not exploit the people. The narrative arc and perspective control belong to Nehemiah as the person in authority responding to the people's grievances, not to the working people themselves.
